requests.title: PA-1400 Multi-Gig speed and duplex configuration semantics
known_facts: The current official English PA-1400 front-panel page lists 2.5G and 5G physical rates for these ports but does not specify whether speed and duplex settings are auto-only.
The official Simplified Chinese PA-1400 hardware PDF, copyright 2023, says RJ45 speed and duplex are auto-negotiated only; its applicability to current hardware and PAN-OS trains is unknown.
Physical rates do not establish configurable values, exported XML, or defaults. The source difference is unresolved, not a proven contradiction.
unresolved_questions: Are link-speed and link-duplex auto-only on PA-1410 ethernet1/9-1/12 and PA-1420 ethernet1/5-1/12? Answer each field independently.
If manual speed is allowed, what exact accepted configuration value represents 2.5G and what exported XML is produced?
If manual speed is allowed, what exact accepted configuration value represents 5G and what exported XML is produced?
For default/auto speed, is link-speed omitted, explicitly auto, or represented otherwise in exported and accepted XML?
For default/auto duplex, is link-duplex omitted, explicitly auto, or represented otherwise in exported and accepted XML?
If manual speed or duplex is unsupported, are such nodes rejected, ignored, normalized to auto, preserved but functionally ignored, or handled another way?
Are the answers identical for PA-1410 and PA-1420, and for PoE-capable versus non-PoE Multi-Gig groups with respect only to speed and duplex?
Do answers vary across PAN-OS 11.0, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1.2+, and 12.2; what are exact boundaries?
Which current authoritative behavior reconciles the English page's silence and the 2023 Chinese reference's auto-only wording?
requested_vendor_artifacts: Official exact-model, exact-train sanitized exported XML for default/auto and, if supported, manual 2.5G and 5G speed and duplex
Official Engineering or TAC model/port/PAN-OS behavior matrix and authoritative documentation revision

acceptance_criteria.SUFFICIENT: Verifiable official answer resolves auto-only versus manual capability; if manual, exact 2.5G/5G values and exported XML; independent speed and duplex defaults, accepted/failure behavior, exact model/port/train scope, and the source discrepancy, enough for deterministic renderer design.
acceptance_criteria.PARTIAL: Some requested semantics or model/port/train applicability remain unanswered, including a reply that gives only physical rates or only speed.
acceptance_criteria.CONFLICTING: Verifiable official responses assert incompatible behavior for the same model, port, and train.

insufficient_response_examples: A generic CLI syntax or GUI screenshot without exact model, version, and exported XML.
requests.submission_body: We are validating configuration migration behavior between supported Palo Alto Networks firewall models and need authoritative confirmation of exact PAN-OS configuration semantics. For PA-1410 ethernet1/9-1/12 and PA-1420 ethernet1/5-1/12 on PAN-OS 11.0, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1.2+, and 12.2, are link-speed and link-duplex independently auto-only? The current English PA-1400 front-panel page lists 2.5G/5G physical rates but is silent on this restriction; an official Simplified Chinese PA-1400 PDF copyrighted 2023 says RJ45 speed and duplex are auto-negotiated only. Please clarify the currently authoritative model/version behavior without assuming a contradiction. If manual speed is supported, specify the exact accepted 2.5G and 5G values and exported XML for each. For both speed and duplex, specify whether default/auto is an omitted node, explicit auto, or another XML representation; explain rejection, normalization, ignoring, or preservation of unsupported manual values. Please identify differences between PA-1410 and PA-1420, PoE-capable and non-PoE Multi-Gig groups only as to link settings, and PAN-OS trains. An official exact-model sanitized XML export and/or Engineering model/port/version matrix would resolve this. No customer configuration is included.
response_intake_requirements: Verify official provenance, response date, responder role, exact models, ports, and PAN-OS versions.

Sanitize before any repository entry; retain safe technical statement, public URL or private-source marker, and artifact hash/reference while excluding customer details, credentials, serials, personal contacts, and private case URLs.
Evaluate all acceptance criteria; do not change evidence or renderer support from request status alone.
requests.notes: PoE configuration semantics belong to a separate P1 gap. No request was submitted or answered.

Independently, is default/auto link-duplex omitted, explicit <link-duplex>auto</link-duplex>, or another accepted/exported representation?
What happens to a manual link-speed node: rejection, ignoring, normalization to auto, preservation without effect, or another documented behavior?
Independently, what happens to a manual link-duplex node?
Are these answers identical on PA-3220, PA-3250, and PA-3260; if not, what differs?
Are these answers identical across PAN-OS 10.1, 10.2, 11.0, and 11.1; if not, identify exact version boundaries.
